Name: Door Furniture
Author: aedenthorn
Description:
[youtube]-deHuwqq9dc[/youtube]

[b][size=5][u]Overview[/u][/size][/b]

This mod does the following:

[list]
[*]Adds (non-lockable) wooden and metal doors as furniture that can be crafted or purchased.[/*]
[*]Provides an optional download that adds lockable wooden and metal doors as furniture that can be crafted or purchased.[/*]
[*]Adds config options to change crafting and purchasing cost for the added doors.[/*]
[*]Adds a very simple means for modders to create their own optionally-lockable door furniture.[/*]
[*]Implements door coloring and a custom color picker.[/*]
[*]Implements custom door furniture descriptions (the game does not normally allow custom furniture descriptions).[/*]
[*]Implements door opening, closing, locking and unlocking by players.[/*]
[*]Implements custom bounding boxes for doors, so players only collide with the door frame itself, rather than the entire tile.[/*]
[*]Implements proper door animation for all four possible rotations as well as flipping for a total of eight possible positions per door.[/*]
[*]Causes NPCs to open and close doors when walking through them.[/*]
[*]Provides options for door auto-open and door auto-close after a specified delay.[/*]
[*]Adds a door key item type for lockable doors and a key ring item type for key management.[/*]
[*]Adds key naming, renaming, and copying.[/*]
[/list]

[b][size=5][u]Basic Usage[/u][/size][/b]

You can craft wooden doors using 10 wood and 5 hardwood or purchase them for 2000g from Robin.

You can craft metal doors using 10 iron bars and 5 refined quartz or purchase them for 5000g from Robin.

You can change the requrired ingredients and price in the config. Setting empty ingredients or negative price removes the item from crafting and purchasing respectively.

Holding a door, you can rotate it as with any other furniture. To flip the door, press the flip keybind (default [b]F[/b]) while holding it.

After the door is placed, interacting with it will cause it to open or close. Doors that are not locked can be picked up like any other furniture.

To change the color of a placed door, either hover over the door and scroll with the mouse or press the color keybind (default [b]C[/b]) to open a custom color picker.


[b][size=5][u]Lockable Doors[/u][/size][/b]

The main mod file doesn't include any lockable doors, but adds full support for lockable doors. There is an optional file that adds two lockable doors that are otherwise identical to the two ordinary doors (apart from being named as lockable).

To lock a lockable door, walk up to it and press the lock keybind (default [b]L[/b]). You must be facing and right next to a door to lock or unlock it.

The first time you lock a door, it will give you a key and open a key naming menu to name the key. Keys only work on the door they were created for.

Locked doors cannot be picked up.

To unlock a lockable door, walk up to the locked door and press the lock key. The corresponding key (or key on a key ring) must be in the player inventory to unlock a door.

Keys can be combined using the combine keybind (default [b]middle mouse button[/b]), which turns them into a key ring. In an inventory, hold one key (or key ring), hover over another key (or key ring), and press the combine keybind.

To uncombine a key ring, hover over it while not holding anything, and press the combine keybind.

To make a copy of a door key, hover over it in an inventory and press the copy keybind (default [b]C[/b]).

To rename a door key, hover over it in an inventory and press the rename keybind (default [b]R[/b]).


[b][size=5][u]Automation[/u][/size][/b]

You can set global automation for doors in the config.

Doors can be set to open automatically on collision. NPCs will automatically open doors when colliding with them (unless they are locked).

Doors can be set to close automatically after a delay in the config. NPCs will automatically close doors after 10 game ticks (can be changed in confg).

Automatic door closing timers only count down when no player or NPC is in range of the door.


[b][size=5][u]Custom Door Sprites[/u][/size][/b]

To change the sprite for the two doors added by this mod, just target their sprite path using Content Patcher's EditImage function:

[b]"aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_door"[/b]

To change the sprite for the default key and key ring items, target their sprite path using Content Patcher's EditImage function:

[b]"aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_key"[/b]


[b][size=5][u]Custom Doors[/u][/size][/b]

Creating basic custom doors is very simple.

First, create your custom door furniture using content patcher, e.g.:

[code]        {
            "Action": "EditData",
            "Target": "Data/Furniture",
            "Entries": {
                "aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_door3": "aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_door3/door/1 3/1 1/4/100/2/{{i18n:aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_door3}}/0/aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_door/true"
            }
        },[/code]

Second, give your door furniture a sprite. This is the most difficult part, since the sprite needs three frames that are not identical to vanilla game sprites (for rotation 2 where the door knob is on the opposite side of the door). You can use the sprite below for reference:

[img width=256]https://github.com/aedenthorn/StardewValleyMods/blob/master/DoorFurniture/assets/door.png?raw=true[/img]

Each door in the sprite requires 8 frames, as follows:

rotation 0, rotation 1 (and 3 flipped), rotation 2, opening frame 1, opening frame 2, rotation 2 opening frame 1, rotation 2 opening frame 2, rotation 2 opened frame.

If the door is colorable, you need to add greyscale overlays as above.

Tell Content Patcher about your sprite as usual, e.g.:

[code]        {
            "Action": "Load",
            "Target": "aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_door",
            "FromFile": "assets/door.png"
        },[/code]
Third, tell this mod about your door furniture using Content Patcher, e.g.:

[code]        {
            "Action": "EditData",
            "Target": "aedenthorn.DoorFurniture/dict",
            "Entries": {
                "aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_door3": {},
            }
        },[/code]
And that's it!

For advanced custom doors, you can add many different fields to the dictionary entry, e.g.:

[code]        {
            "Action": "EditData",
            "Target": "aedenthorn.DoorFurniture/dict",
            "Entries": {
                "aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_door": {
                    "Bounds": [
                        {
                            "X": 0,
                            "Y": 48,
                            "Width": 64,
                            "Height": 16
                        },
                        {
                            "X": 48,
                            "Y": 0,
                            "Width": 16,
                            "Height": 64
                        },
                        {
                            "X": 0,
                            "Y": 0,
                            "Width": 64,
                            "Height": 16
                        },
                        {
                            "X": 0,
                            "Y": 0,
                            "Width": 16,
                            "Height": 64
                        }
                    ],
                    "Type": "Door",
                    "Description": "Can be opened and closed.",
                    "KeyItem": "aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_key",
                    "KeyRingItem": "aedenthorn.DoorFurniture_keyring",
                    "OpenSound": "doorOpen",
                    "CloseSound": "doorClose",
                    "LockSound": "openBox",
                    "UnlockSound": "openBox",
                    "Lockable": false,
                    "AutoOpen": false,
                    "AutoCloseDelay": -1,
                   "ColorSpriteOffset": {
                        "X": 0,
                        "Y": 96
                    },
                    "Colorable": true,
                    "DefaultUncolored": true,
                    "DefaultColor": {
                        "B": 0,
                        "G": 0,
                        "R": 0,
                        "A": 255
                    },
                    "Colors": null
                }
            }
        },[/code]
All fields can safely be omitted.

Field explanation is as follows:

[list]
[*][b]Bounds[/b] - the collision bounds in pixels, one for each door rotation.[/*]
[*][b]Type[/b] - used for the colored text to display as the category in tooltips.[/*]
[*][b]Description[/b] - to be shown in place of generic furniture description in tooltips.[/*]
[*][b]KeyItem[/b] - the ItemId of the type of item to use as a key for this type of door.[/*]
[*][b]KeyRingItem[/b] - the ItemId of the type of item to use as a key ring for this type of door's keys.[/*]
[*][b]OpenSound[/b] - played when the door opens.[/*]
[*][b]CloseSound[/b] - played when the door closed.[/*]
[*][b]LockSound[/b] - played when the door is locked.[/*]
[*][b]UnlockSound[/b] - played when the door is unlocked.[/*]
[*][b]AutoOpen[/b] - whether the door should auto-open when players collide with it, irrespective of the mod's config setting.[/*]
[*][b]AutoCloseDelay[/b] - how many game ticks to wait before auto-closing the door (negative values means it won't auto-close.[/*]
[*][b]Colorable[/b] - whether this door is colorable (requires greyscale overlay in the spritesheet).[/*]
[*][b]ColorSpriteOffset[/b] - how far away in x-y pixels the greyscale overlay is from the uncolored sprite on the sprite sheet.[/*]
[*][b]DefaultColor[/b] - a color to assign to  (or use as a placeholder for) a colorable door that is not colored.[/*]
[*][b]DefaultUncolored[/b] - whether the default color should instead show the uncolored sprite.[/*]
[*][b]Colors[/b] - a custom list of colors to allow the door to be painted as. Each entry should have "R","G", and "B" values. Without this list, the game's chest colors will be used.[/*]
[/list]

[b][size=5][u]Mod Config[/u][/size][/b]

You can use GMCM to edit the config variables. Options include:

[list]
[*]Global auto-open and close settings[/*]
[*]Door crafting and purchasing costs[/*]
[*]Keybinds[/*]
[*]Text Colors[/*]
[/list]
[b][size=5][u]Limitations[/u][/size][/b]

First, remember these are not map tiles, they are furniture. So, before I get asked a million times, no they won't magically recolor based on your map recolor mod. Fortunately, you can easily implement your own doors, or just change the sprite for the default doors as explained above.

NPCs do not respect locked doors - they will just walk through them; I think the alternative is probably not viable due to their schedules.


[u][size=5][b]Technical[/b][/size][/u]

Requires SMAPI.

Implements a [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] interface to change config settings in-game. If you have [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10505]GMCM Options[/url], you can also change the colors in-game.

Code is at [url=https://github.com/aedenthorn/StardewValleyMods]https://github.com/aedenthorn/StardewValleyMods[/url].

A list of all my mods for Stardew Valley is available at [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/articles/895]https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/articles/895[/url].
